title: Frequency-Based Matcher for Long-Tailed Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: One-to-many query matching where the number of queries matched to each class is set from class frequency, to stop oversuppression of rare classes in mask transformers; also a long-tailed seg benchmark with a dual (frequent vs rare) metric.
adaptation: In a mask classifier on our 24 classes, give inactive, splice, corrosion, material several matched queries per image; report frequent-class and rare-class mIoU separately (fits mIoU_rob vs all-class).
min_experiment: M2F arm B vs B + frequency-based matching, 5-fold CV; metric inactive IoU and mean IoU over rare classes (splice, material, edge_dark, corrosion); kill if rare-class mIoU gain < 0.02.
evidence: R: abstract only (TMM 2024); tail-class numbers not retrieved; code promised, unverified.
prior_overlap: none: long-tail losses and matching never tried.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: report head and tail classes separately in our per-class tables. Matcher only if a Mask2Former-type decoder is adopted.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No training run; adopt head/tail split reporting in the benchmark scorer and recompute existing runs.
